# Marcus Lee

I ran into Marcus in the kitchen this morning while I was making coffee and he was packing his lunch for work. We chatted about the usual stuff - how his latest project at the firm is going, whether the new protein powder he bought tastes any good, and if the traffic on 35 was as bad as it looked on the app. He's been my roommate for almost two years now and honestly it's been one of the easiest living situations I've had. We just kind of vibe without needing to force anything.

Marcus is my main climbing partner these days. We try to hit the gym together [[Bouldering Project]] every Tuesday and Friday evening unless one of us has a deadline or is traveling. Those sessions have become pretty sacred. Sometimes we push each other on the harder V4s and V5s, other times we just mess around on the slabs and talk about whatever. He's way better at dynos than I am, but I usually edge him out on the technical footwork stuff. It's a good balance.

I still owe him $62 for the day passes we bought last month when my membership was glitching. I keep forgetting to send it. His Venmo is @marcus-lee-88. I should really just do it tonight before it slips my mind again. He's never made it weird, but I hate being the flaky one on stuff like that.

We were talking last night about his upcoming move. He's heading to Seattle in August for a big promotion at his company. It's bittersweet. On one hand I'm really happy for him - it's what he's been working toward for the last year and a half. On the other, I'm going to miss having my default climbing buddy and someone to split rent and argue over what to watch on Netflix with. Finding a new roommate is going to be a whole thing. Finding a new regular climbing partner might be even harder.

He's already started boxing up some of his gear in the living room. I saw his old pair of La Sportiva shoes sitting on top of a box yesterday and it hit me that our Tuesday/Friday routine is only going to last another six or seven weeks. We joked about doing a big send-off trip to Hueco or something before he leaves, but we both know neither of us has the vacation time for that right now. Maybe we'll at least squeeze in an extra session or two.

Marcus has this dry sense of humor that sneaks up on you. He'll say something completely deadpan about the guy who just fell off the V3 and then go right back to chalking up like nothing happened. I think that's why we get along so well. Neither of us needs constant entertainment or small talk. We can sit in the van after a session just listening to a podcast and it's not awkward.

I need to remember to ask him if he's found a place in Seattle yet. Last I heard he was debating between Capitol Hill and Ballard. Also should probably start thinking about what to do with the spare climbing rope we've been sharing. Maybe I'll buy him a six-pack of his favorite IPA as a partial thank you for putting up with my mess in the bathroom for two years.

The apartment is going to feel pretty quiet without him.

[[Sam Thompson]]
